evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep said "I just need ten to fifteen minutes of your time if that's okay?" but did NOT wait for explicit confirmation before moving to "Before I proceed, so I just like to know aside from the pricing, do you have any other concerns?" — framing was present but rushed past without a clear yes.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Asked "aside from the pricing, do you have any other concerns about the moving process?" but only AFTER the customer had already raised the availability concern in the opening exchange — this was reactive, not proactive discovery.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: When customer raised availability concern ("wondering if there's any availability tomorrow"), rep said "Mm-hmm alright, I go and check that for you" and immediately put them on hold — no follow-up like "tell me more about why tomorrow is important" or understanding the underlying need.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Rep confirmed: pickup address (5100 Road, Austin 7871), property type (1BR apartment, 700 sq ft), items (bookshelf, day bed, credenza, 10 boxes), floor/elevator access (4th floor with elevator), walking distance from parking (150 feet), delivery address (851 Airport Boulevard, 5x10 storage unit, 2nd floor).
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Not asked — rep discussed moving blanket deposit ($14) but never offered packing services ("Would you like us to pack your items into boxes for you?").
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Not asked — no mention of typical box count, overflow check, or china/book collection verification despite customer already mentioning 10 boxes.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep gave hourly rate ($110/hour per mover, $220 total, 2.5-hour minimum = $550) but did NOT anchor to a typical range for a 700 sq ft one-bedroom or personalize based on customer's stated concerns (availability stress, budget sensitivity).
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Trip fee/overnight fee NOT disclosed upfront. Minimum 2.5-hour framing WAS mentioned ("for every move Sophie, we do have a minimum of two and a half hours"). No mention of 15-minute increments or "not a guess" framing.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Rep never asked "Does that feel fair?" — moved straight from quoting $550 to discussing moving blanket options, then customer objected on price and call ended.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No reflection or confirmation loop — rep launched into moving blanket discussion immediately after pricing.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Never asked — when customer said "I think there's, yeah. Okay. There might be a couple of things I want to protect just like the day bed actually," rep treated this as a blanket preference, not a final concern check.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Never asked "Would you like our help with your move?" — customer objected on price and ended the call; rep said "yes, I understand ma'am. Mm-hmm thank you for consideration and have a good day." No attempt to recover or close.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Not confirmed — call ended without any booking details (date, phone, arrival window, crew size, addresses, notes) because customer rejected on price before rep attempted any close.

top_strength: Jeline gathered all core logistics details cleanly (property type, floor access, walking distance, furniture and box inventory, destination) and confirmed them back to the customer with precision — no gaps in the discovery foundation.
coaching_note: Move Section 2's concerns check ("any other concerns?") to the very beginning BEFORE availability discussion, then two-layer deep every concern the customer raises; omit Sections 5 (Two Promises) and 7 (explicit ask/close) entirely on this call because pricing landed at $550 for a small move and customer rejected before you had a chance to reframe value or recover — the real miss was never offering packing services upfront or asking about overflow, which might have reset the perceived value, and then not anchoring the price to typical ranges before quoting.
